notes: generateRegistrationOptions() with only rpName/rpID/userName. Defaults read from v14.0.3 source: algs [-8,-7,-257] (EdDSA first), 32-byte random challenge and 32-byte random user.id, timeout 60000, attestation 'none', userDisplayName defaults to the EMPTY STRING, credProps:true always merged into extensions, hints always emitted (empty array), excludeCredentials always emitted. Because the default authenticatorSelection has residentKey 'preferred', the library also sets requireResidentKey:false. Rp/user strings are illustrative.

rp: SimpleWebAuthn @simplewebauthn/server v14.0.3 on a runtime with WebCrypto ML-DSA-44
notes: Same defaults as simplewebauthn-v14-create-default, but getDefaultSupportedAlgorithmIDs() prepends ML-DSA-44 (-48) when SettingsService.runtimeSupportsPQC() detects WebCrypto 'ML-DSA-44' support. The most preferred algorithm is a post-quantum one; an authenticator that only does ES256 must skip -48 and -8.

generateAuthenticationOptions({rpID}) only. allowCredentials and extensions are undefined and therefore absent after JSON serialization (discoverable flow); 32-byte challenge; timeout 60000; UV 'preferred'.

generate_registration_options(rp_id, rp_name, user_name) serialized with options_to_json_dict(). 64-byte challenge AND 64-byte user handle (the maximum user.id size), displayName defaults to user_name, no authenticatorSelection, no extensions, hints omitted (None). The matching get default is {challenge: 64 bytes, timeout: 60000, rpId, allowCredentials: [], userVerification: 'preferred'} -- an explicit empty allowCredentials list rather than an absent one.

Hard-coded in createPublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions(): EdDSA/ES256/RS256, residentKey 'required' (no requireResidentKey member is serialized), UV 'preferred', 5-minute timeout serialized as 300000 ms, Bytes.random() = 32 bytes for both challenge and new user ids, name and displayName are both the authenticated principal name. Get default: allowCredentials = the user's credentials, 32-byte challenge, rpId, timeout 300000, UV 'preferred'.

preferredPubkeyParams default = ES256, EdDSA, ES384, ES512, Ed448 (-53, fully-specified), RS256, RS384, RS512, ML-DSA-44/65/87 (-48/-49/-50), then filterAvailableAlgorithms() drops any alg without a JCA KeyFactory: on Java 17/21 the ML-DSA entries disappear (8 algs); this entry assumes Java 24+. 32-byte challenge. timeout and authenticatorSelection are absent unless set (Jackson NON_ABSENT keeps empty lists, so hints:[] and excludeCredentials:[] are emitted). credProps is always merged in; appidExclude is added only when RelyingParty.appId is configured (U2F migration). toCredentialsCreateJson() wraps this in {"publicKey": ...}. user.id is application-supplied (32 bytes here).

CredentialParametersDefault() = ES256, ES384, ES512, RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, EdDSA (EdDSA last, RSA-PSS included). 32-byte challenge; timeout 300000 (120000 when UV is 'discouraged'); attestation, authenticatorSelection, extensions, hints and an empty excludeCredentials are all omitted (omitempty/omitzero). Server JSON is wrapped as {"publicKey": {...}, "mediation"?}. user.id is User.WebAuthnID() (1-64 bytes; 32 here). Config.EncodeUserIDAsString=true makes the server emit user.id as the raw string instead of base64url. Alternative presets: CredentialParametersRecommendedL3 = [-8,-7,-257]; CredentialParametersPQCRecommendedL3 = [-48,-49,-50,-8,-7,-257].

Only ES256+RS256 (COSEAlgorithm::secure_algs(); no EdDSA). user.id is the caller's UUID as 16 raw bytes. Passkey registration paradoxically sends residentKey 'discouraged' with UV 'required'. Extensions include the credProtect inputs (credentialProtectionPolicy/enforceCredentialProtectionPolicy, flattened into extensions) and the legacy 'uvm' extension. Server JSON is wrapped as {"publicKey": ...}; excludeCredentials/hints are omitted when None.

start_discoverable_authentication() forces RequestChallengeResponse.mediation = Conditional and sends an explicit empty allowCredentials with the 'uvm' extension. The mediation member travels next to publicKey in the server JSON ({"publicKey": ..., "mediation": "conditional"}).

Verbatim JSON pasted in the issue (Apr 2025). hints contains the INVALID value 'securitykey' (0.5.1 serialized the enum without the hyphen; 0.5.2 uses kebab-case 'security-key'); unknown hint values must be ignored. Chrome rejected this request with NotSupportedError because credProtect 'userVerificationRequired' is combined with userVerification 'preferred'. localhost RP ID over http.

PubKeyCredParam.Defaults = EdDSA, ES256, RS256, PS256, ES384, RS384, PS384, ES512, RS512, PS512; Fido2Configuration.ChallengeSize = 16 bytes (the spec minimum); Timeout 60000; AuthenticatorSelection.Default = residentKey 'preferred' + UV 'discouraged'; attestationFormats [] and hints [] always serialized; extensions omitted when null. user.id is caller-supplied (1-64 bytes enforced). Bitwarden (a fido2-net-lib user) sent [-7,-257,-37,-35,-258,-38,-36,-259,-39,-8] in 2024, i.e. EdDSA last.

Default realm policy leaves everything 'not specified', so the page passes ONLY challenge, rp, user and pubKeyCredParams: no attestation, no authenticatorSelection, no timeout (createTimeout 0), no excludeCredentials (avoidSameAuthenticatorRegister=false). rp.name defaults to 'keycloak'; rp.id defaults to the request host. user.id is base64url(UTF-8 of the Keycloak user UUID string) = 36 ASCII bytes; displayName is the USERNAME. Challenge is webauthn4j DefaultChallenge(): 16 bytes from a random UUID (version/variant bits fixed). Keycloak < 22 (before PR keycloak/keycloak#20832, June 2023) passed alg values as STRINGS. The passwordless/passkey policy (WebAuthnPolicyPasswordlessDefaults) instead adds authenticatorSelection {residentKey:'required', requireResidentKey:true, userVerification:'required'}.

doAuthenticate() builds {rpId, challenge} and adds allowCredentials ([] for the conditional flow) and userVerification (passwordless policy default 'required'); timeout omitted because createTimeout defaults to 0. mediation comes from the realm (default 'conditional'; 'optional'/'required' are also supported) and an AbortSignal is always passed. 16-byte UUID-derived challenge.

Browser-side library: register({challenge, user:'user'}). rp.id AND rp.name both default to window.location.hostname; user.id defaults to crypto.randomUUID() converted char-by-char (36 ASCII bytes; non-Latin-1 ids would be truncated by charCodeAt); displayName defaults to name. attestation defaults to 'direct' (option attestation=true). timeout, userVerification, hints and authenticatorAttachment are passed through as undefined (absent here) despite the JSDoc claiming 60000/'required' defaults.

CoseKey.supported_algorithms() = ES256, EdDSA, ES384, ES512, PS256, RS256, ES256K (-47, secp256k1); ML-DSA-44/65/87 are appended when the cryptography backend supports them. Fido2Server sets timeout=None and attestation=None, and authenticatorSelection/excludeCredentials are only emitted when passed, so the default is the minimal 4-member dictionary. 32-byte challenge; user entity is caller-supplied. Server output is {"publicKey": ...}. python-fido2 0.9.x (pinned by Sentry at the 2024 commit cited in sentry-create-cbor-zero-padded-userid) defaulted to [-7,-8,-37,-257].

Derived from GitLab's open-source controller (webauthn-ruby 3.x): rp has NO id (config.rp_id is not set), so the browser uses the page's effective domain. Algs = webauthn-ruby default ['ES256','PS256','RS256'] -> [-7,-37,-257] (the same list Shopify, Stripe and Sony send). user.id = webauthn_xid = 64 random bytes; 32-byte challenge; timeout 300000 (gem default). GitLab sets config.encoding = :base64, so challenge/user.id travel as STANDARD base64 with padding and GitLab's JS converts them (re-encoded to base64url here). Requires residentKey but sets no requireResidentKey. 2FA (non-passkey) registration uses {userVerification:'discouraged', residentKey:'preferred'}.

options_for_get(allow: ids, user_verification: 'discouraged'). config.legacy_u2f_appid = the GitLab base URL, so EVERY get carries extensions.appid (an origin URL, not a JSON facets file) -- including passkey sign-in, which uses allowCredentials [] + userVerification 'required'. rpId is ABSENT (relying_party.id is nil). Credential ids have no transports. Ids/challenge are placeholders (64-byte ids assumed); wire encoding is standard base64 (config.encoding = :base64).

KeePassXC-Browser debug log, Oct 2026 (values REDACTED in the source). Non-standard Chromium-only extension input googleLegacyAppidSupport (false here; CloakBrowser #505 says the older post-sign-in enrollment flow sent googleLegacyAppidSupport:true without appidExclude). appidExclude points at the gstatic origins.json U2F facet list, which Chromium special-cases for Google domains. rp.id google.com is a parent domain of the page host. Corbado (2024) saw the same alg list/attestation and excludeCredentials carrying all five transports [usb,nfc,ble,hybrid,internal]; this 2026 capture has no transports. Captured by the Fidentikit crawler (Oct 2025, two identical-shape captures) by instrumenting navigator.credentials.get. 124-byte structured challenge (both captures start 00 FD 89 57). PRF eval.first is the 20-byte ASCII string 'GoogleSignInPrfInput' (not 32 bytes). No allowCredentials and no userVerification (discoverable). timeout 600000. The crawler did not record mediation or the page URL; the origin is inferred (the trigger was a Gmail help-page 'create a passkey' link, and the census paper reports google.com calls get({mediation:'conditional'}) on page load).

KeePassXC-Browser log, Oct 2026, page https://accounts.google.com/v3/signin/challenge/pk/presend. The log showed transports ['cable','internal','internal']; KeePassXC-Browser appends 'internal' to every allowCredentials entry, so Google sent ['cable','internal'] -- 'cable' is the pre-standard name of 'hybrid' and is not in the AuthenticatorTransport enum. The extension also adds enterpriseAttestationPossible:false and rewrites a missing timeout to 30000; both were dropped here. Placeholders: challenge (124 bytes assumed), credential id (16 bytes assumed).

Corbado's captured table (2024). rp.id login.microsoft.com is cross-site from the account.live.com page and is authorized via Related Origin Requests: https://login.microsoft.com/.well-known/webauthn lists login.live.com, login.microsoftonline.com and account.live.com (fetched 2026-10-27). Challenge length unknown (32 assumed). Origin inferred from the KeePassXC thread (account.live.com/proofs/manage/additional).

rp: Okta Identity Engine (Okta Sign-In Widget) security key enrollment
notes: activationData captured with the debugger (Nov 2023, values '[REDACTED]'). The widget passes _.extend({}, activationData, {challenge, user, excludeCredentials}) straight to create(), so the publicKey dictionary carries the NON-STANDARD member u2fParams {appid} and an rp WITHOUT id (defaults to the org host). excludeCredentials is rebuilt client-side from enrolled authenticators (and forced to [] when requireResidentKey is true). Derived from Sentry's source (python-fido2 0.9.2): user.id = user.id.to_bytes(64, 'big'), a 64-byte big-endian integer that is almost entirely ZERO bytes (example integer is synthetic); name and displayName are the username; no timeout/attestation. The server CBOR-encodes {publicKey: ...} and the page decodes it with cbor-web, so every buffer is a Uint8Array VIEW (non-zero byteOffset) into one larger ArrayBuffer: Bitwarden read the whole backing buffer and reported user.id lengths of 589 (Sentry) and 465 (Gandi) bytes. Authentication uses U2FFido2Server, which adds extensions.appid (Sentry's /auth/2fa/u2fappid.json URL).

The page runs PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON(), and the logged result (Edge 149) had DROPPED exts and attestationFormats and ADDED enforceCredentialProtectionPolicy:false (IDL default) -- an intercepting extension sees that shape. The 10-alg order is not visible in the log; fido2-net-lib 4.x default order is assumed.

rp: WebAuthn Level 3 spec PRF test vectors
notes: No production RP using evalByCredential was found (Mozilla accounts, Teleport and BitGo client code accept it but their servers send eval only). The prf input is the spec test vector: eval with first+second (4-byte salts) plus evalByCredential keyed by base64url credential id; the spec requires every key to match an allowCredentials id (SyntaxError otherwise) and evalByCredential needs a non-empty allowCredentials. challenge/rpId/allowCredentials wrapper is synthetic.

Options a developer used against Bitwarden iOS (Jul 2025): EdDSA-ONLY pubKeyCredParams (no -7/-257). Bitwarden and Apple Passwords still created ES256 keys, which the RP then rejects; the spec requires NotSupportedError when no listed alg is supported. Also: mediation 'required', hints, attestationFormats, empty extensions object. user.id and challenge are new Uint8Array(16) (all zeros) as written in the report. No production site without ES256 was found; Nintendo (no RS256), Amazon/Wikipedia (ES256 only) and AgeKey (ML-DSA first) are the closest real ones.

The page builds options with @github/webauthn-json's schema converter (32-byte random challenge and user.id), the same library github.com uses.

rp: Developer test integration (Firefox bug report; RP name 'test.com')
notes: Weak evidence, kept because no production capture of a string challenge was found: the options a developer pasted (May 2024) show challenge and user.id as plain STRINGS that are not base64url of anything meaningful ('testchanllengevalue' happens to be valid base64url text; '12345-543212-12345-54321' contains only base64url characters but is 24 chars). Treat as a negative/robustness fixture: a real create() would need BufferSources and throws TypeError for strings, while a JSON-driven harness would silently base64url-decode these strings -- to reproduce the bug, pass them as raw JS strings to an intercepted create(). Also shows rp without id and a 20 s timeout.
